rows.question: What information do people actually remember about a photo?
rows.restated: What kinds of details do people actually remember about a photo (what, when, who, where, event, etc.)?
rows.gap: the two AI coders agreed too little on question 2.1 to report it as a finding
rows.text:
People most often recall a loose “what” about the photo, with “when” also common, and “where” less so [[analysis_derived|cue_remembered:what:core]] [[analysis_derived|cue_remembered:when:core]] [[analysis_derived|cue_remembered:where:core]].

21% (24 of 115) mention “when,” 10% (11 of 115) mention “where,” while 11% (13 of 115) explicitly say they forgot “when” and 3% (4 of 115) forgot “where” [[analysis_derived|cue_remembered:when:core]] [[analysis_derived|cue_remembered:where:core]] [[analysis_derived|cue_forgotten:when:core]] [[analysis_derived|cue_forgotten:where:core]].

One person trying to prove a timeline said they had "a photo of nagito's bare ass from whenever that episode of the dr3 anime came out" saved, pointing to remembered “what” and a fuzzy “when” [[story|6b5b098ff4054dff58acb46b2aff57a17fe9f25a:0]].

Interpretation: Shares about remembered details are directional because the two AI coders agreed too little on question 2.1 [[analysis_method_flags|low_reliability_fields]].

*Want to see how this splits by kind of photo?*

rows.question: What information have people forgotten about the photo they want?
rows.restated: Which details do people report forgetting about the photo they were trying to find?
rows.text:
People most often forgot when the photo was taken, occasionally where, and in adjacent stories, which app or account held it [[analysis_derived|cue_forgotten:when:core]], [[analysis_derived|cue_forgotten:where:core]], [[analysis_crosstab|adjacent.q:2.4=which_app_or_account@photo_class:_all]].
11% (13 of 115) mentioned the date or year; 3% (4 of 115) the exact place or venue name; and 26% (57 of 216) in adjacent stories named which app or account [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:2.4=date_or_year@photo_class:_all]], [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:2.4=exact_place_or_venue_name@photo_class:_all]], [[analysis_crosstab|adjacent.q:2.4=which_app_or_account@photo_class:_all]].
One story sums up the memory gap: "Obviously, absolutely no one at this point remembers the name of the original photo" [[story|21e3bb4e9ec67356485124747d751c71f31d0ce2:0]].
Interpretation: These are shares of public stories, not user rates [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]].

rows.question: How do users formulate searches when their memory is incomplete?
rows.restated: How do people phrase their search queries when their memory about a photo is incomplete (i.e., what shapes do their first queries take)?
rows.text:
People start with sparse, literal queries — most often a single noun. [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:4.1=single_noun@photo_class:_all]]

The clearest pattern is single-noun first queries at 17% (19 of 115), with smaller shares for several keywords 3% (4 of 115), full natural descriptions 1% (1 of 115), and named entities 1% (1 of 115). [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:4.1=single_noun@photo_class:_all]] [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:4.1=several_keywords@photo_class:_all]] [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:4.1=full_natural_description@photo_class:_all]] [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:4.1=named_entity@photo_class:_all]]

One person begins broad, then struggles to qualify: "I couldn't qualify my results with 'me, selfie' even as half decent." [[story|6b5a4912de3cd10b2ccf2f07757bc417ca500253:1]]

Interpretation: People often forget “when” and anchor on “what,” aligning with remembered what at 41% (47 of 115) and forgotten when at 11% (13 of 115). [[analysis_derived|cue_remembered:what:core]] [[analysis_derived|cue_forgotten:when:core]]

Shares reflect coded public stories, not user success rates. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]

*Want to see how this splits by kind of photo?*

rows.question: Does Google Photos fail to understand the clues people give it?
rows.restated: Do stories in the corpus show that Google Photos failed to understand or match the clues people gave it (stage 5)?
rows.text:
Yes — many public stories say search did not understand what they typed [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:_all]].
27% (31 of 115) of core stories first went wrong at search’s understanding and matching [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:_all]].
One person wrote, "“Two faces” yielded nothing" and "“Black and White” doesn’t work" [[story|3b53d4e5bf5f572ac92dce7bbc1051e9491c662a:0]].
Interpretation: Within those, coders saw concrete failure modes: irrelevant results [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:5.6=irrelevant_results@photo_class:_all]], zero results [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:5.6=zero_results@photo_class:_all]], concept not modelled [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:5.2=concept_not_modelled@photo_class:_all]], wrong date [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:5.2=wrong_date@photo_class:_all]], and items buried below the fold [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:5.4=buried_below_fold@photo_class:_all]] — with similar patterns in adjacent stories [[analysis_crosstab|adjacent.primary_stage=5@photo_class:_all]] — but coverage is thin and stage 5 is inferred [[analysis_method_flags|thin_core]] [[analysis_method_flags|stage5_inferred]].

rows.text:
We can’t answer Android vs iPhone from these stories because device/OS isn’t recorded, so any split by platform would be guesswork [[analysis_method_flags|missing_cuts]].

Interpretation: What we can say is how often “struggle to find” shows up in public stories overall: 27% (31 of 115) in the core set [[analysis_crosstab|share_stage5_core_owners]]. 

One person said “text search Apple photos in the upload widget and be disappointed” before turning to Google Photos to find the image [[story|b7113e3689e0674b9cd8b089fb3bcd093e40d3eb:0]].

rows.question: Has search got worse since Ask Photos launched?
rows.restated: Is Google Photos search worse now than it was before Ask Photos launched?
rows.gap: no before-and-after or over-time comparison was built
rows.text:
We can’t say whether search got worse after Ask Photos launched, because the stories don’t include any before-and-after comparison or dates to anchor change over time [[analysis_method_flags|missing_cuts]]. What we can show is where people say search fails today: search did not understand what they typed (Stage 5) is the most common failure in the core stories [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:_all]].

27% (31 of 115) of core stories first go wrong at Stage 5 [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:_all]].

One person wrote: "It used to find all images that contained whatever keyword I asked for. Now it can't even find the most simple and blatant keywords." [[story|9a7306c83836251e47a6ca073afd34441115de00:0]]

Interpretation: Some posts explicitly claim decline, but without time stamps we can’t tie them to the launch window; and quiet successes do appear too [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=9@photo_class:_all]] [[analysis_method_flags|public_selection_bias]].
